- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially >0.67) — model tends to overshoot in bullish phases.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment (sentiment <0.33) — model fails to recognize bearish momentum.
- Lagged corrections: model often misses early bearish turns; true price drops lag behind forecasted peaks.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, underestimating reversion to prior mean after sharp moves.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate in early bullish sentiment windows, then underestimate in late bearish phases.
- Sentiment-driven adjustment: if sentiment >0.67 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence.
- If sentiment <0.33 for 3+ consecutive days, increase forecast by 1–2% to account for underestimation bias.
- Avoid “peak chasing” — if forecast peaks coincide with sentiment peak, reduce peak value by 1–3% to prevent overshoot.
